claims.text: The as-deposited alloy has composition Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17.
The patterned nanoribbons are 500 µm long, 300 nm wide, and 35 nm thick.
The as-deposited material is amorphous or extremely fine and disordered, with cubic-type short-range order.
The as-deposited surface has Rq approximately 0.79 nm and Ra approximately 0.63 nm.
Annealing at 700 K induces short-range atomic reordering.
Annealing at 700 K relaxes fabrication-induced internal strain.
The 700 K anneal can produce reordering and strain relaxation without generating long-range crystallinity.
Annealing-induced reordering reduces local domain-pinning barriers.
Annealing-induced reordering improves collective exchange interactions.
Reduced pinning and improved exchange increase magnetization and the effective ferromagnetic volume fraction.
Reduced pinning and improved exchange increase the isothermal magnetic entropy change during cooling cycles.
Longitudinal elastic tensile strain up to 2% enhances magnetic order through magnetoelastic coupling above 100 K.
Longitudinal elastic tensile strain strengthens the magnetic response without shifting the blocking-peak position.
Increasing nanoribbon spacing from 1 µm to 2 µm reduces inter-ribbon magnetic coupling.
Reduced inter-ribbon coupling at 2 µm spacing reduces coupling-induced in-plane anisotropy.
The unannealed, unstrained 1 µm-spaced baseline has a maximum −ΔSM of approximately 1.25 J kg−1 K−1 at 140 K for ΔH = 50 kOe.
The 700 K annealed nanoribbons will have a maximum −ΔSM greater than approximately 1.25 J kg−1 K−1 at 140 K for ΔH = 50 kOe.
The relevant magnetocaloric-response region is approximately 40–200 K, with a potentially inverse magnetocaloric effect below 20 K.
